title: How Much Do You Trust A Dog? Quantifying Hint-Following in Reasoning Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.32055v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit sycophancy, altering their answers to align with user suggestions even on objective factual and reasoning tasks. Yet the quantitative form of this influence--- and whether it is calibrated to source reliability--- remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate this behavior through hint-induced answer shifts on MMLU questions, evaluating prompts of the form ``[Source] thinks the answer is (X)''. We systematically vary the source to which the hint is attributed (a professor, a friend, or a dog) across three open-source model families, Qwen, Gemma, and SmolLM. We show that the change induced by the hint follows a predictable structure well-characterized by an exponential tilt: the hint induces an approximately constant mean shift in the hinted answer's log-odds, with question--target susceptibility largely shared across sources. translated_title: 你有多信任一只狗？量化推理语言模型中的提示遵循行为
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）常常表现出谄媚行为，即使在客观的事实和推理任务上，也会为了迎合用户的建议而改变自己的答案。然而，这种影响的定量形式——以及它是否与信息来源的可靠性相校准——仍然知之甚少。在本工作中，我们通过MMLU问题上的提示诱导答案偏移来研究这一行为，评估形如“[来源]认为答案是(X)”的提示。我们在三个开源模型系列（Qwen、Gemma和SmolLM）上系统地改变提示所归属的来源（教授、朋友或狗）。我们表明，提示引起的变化遵循一个可预测的结构，该结构可以用指数倾斜很好地刻画：提示在被提示答案的对数几率上引起近似恒定的均值偏移，且问题与目标的易感性在不同来源之间很大程度上是共享的。为了探索这种模式如何产生，我们引入了一个形式化的……
tldr: 该研究发现大语言模型对提示来源（如教授、朋友甚至狗）的答案偏移遵循可预测的指数倾斜结构，且偏移强度与来源可靠性基本无关，揭示了模型谄媚行为未被来源可靠性校准的问题。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that LLMs' hint-induced answer shifts follow a predictable exponential tilt structure regardless of the hint source (professor, friend, or dog), showing that sycophancy is largely not calibrated to source reliability.
